## Natural history notes

A small brown thrush characterized by a warm reddish-brown tail, spotted white breast, thin pale eye ring, and habit of slowly raising and lowering its tail while perched. In Florida, the Hermit Thrush is mainly a winter visitor and migrant, found in hardwood hammocks, pine woods, forest edges, thickets, parks, yards, and shrubby wetlands. It feeds on insects, spiders, and other small invertebrates on or near the ground, especially in leaf litter, and also eats berries and small fruits during the winter.
